title: Memphis Dry-Rub Pulled Pork
seoTitle: Memphis Dry-Rub Pulled Pork | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Memphis-style pull where the rub does the talking
subtitle: Paprika-coffee rub, no sauce on the meat, and slaw buns for ten
description: Adapted from classic Memphis dry-rub tradition (Amazing Ribs, Meat Church): shoulder gets a bold paprika-coffee rub, smokes without saucing the meat, and serves with tangy slaw on buns—sauce on the side only.

steps.title: Build Memphis rub
steps.instruction: Mix salt, brown sugar, paprika, garlic, onion, cumin, coffee, and pepper. Coat shoulder with mustard, then pack rub on all sides. Rest 30 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke at 250°F
steps.instruction: Smoke shoulder fat-side up at 250°F until bark is mahogany and internal temp reaches 165°F, about 5–6 hours. Do not mop or sauce the meat.

steps.title: Wrap to 203°F
steps.instruction: Wrap in foil when bark is set. Continue at 250°F until probe-tender and 203°F internal, about 2–3 hours.

steps.title: Rest and pull
steps.instruction: Rest wrapped 45 minutes. Pull into a pan with defatted juices only—no sauce mixed in. Keep bark pieces mixed through for texture.

steps.title: Tangy slaw
steps.instruction: Toss slaw with mayo, vinegar, and pinch of salt. Chill until service.

steps.title: Hold at 170°F
steps.instruction: Cover pulled pork with foil and hold at 170°F. Serve sauce on the side in a squeeze bottle.
Dry-rub pork, slaw, buns, optional sauce. Call it Memphis-style—slaw on the sandwich, sauce if you want it.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Reheat covered with a splash of apple juice. Chop into tacos with slaw and hot sauce.

proTips: Coffee in the rub adds depth without making the pork taste like breakfast.
Never sauce the meat before pulling—Memphis style keeps bark intact.
Mix some slaw into the sandwich for the classic contrast of smoky and tangy.
tonightSpread: Pulled pork in a pan with bark visible.
Slaw, buns, and optional sauce on the side.
leftovers: Memphis pork nachos with slaw on top.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Dry-rub pork tastes clean and smoky, not sweet. Holds beautifully at 170°F and lets crews choose their sauce level.
mealPrepNotes: Apply rub the night before if possible. Hold pulled pork covered at 170°F up to 2 hours. Keep sauce separate so bark stays crisp.
